title: Veil and Ember Anew
premise: Petra Joubert, exiled storm-caller, has hidden his magic for seven years in the charm-stalls of Greyhollow, a city where sorcery is punishable by drowning. When the old gods stir and answer prayers again, Petra's dormant inheritance awakens, marking him as the last heir of the storm-line the usurper King Vaelric thought extinguished. To save the free cities from Vaelric's advancing armies, Petra must descend into the court beneath the mountain and steal back the soul of his sister Maerin, sold to the underworld as collateral for their family's old bargain. He succeeds at terrible cost—trading his own name into the ledger in her place—and returns to lead the free cities not as a storm-caller, but as something new: a god-touched mortal whose power belongs to no crown.
about_author: Ada Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked for, usually near the sea.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In Greyhollow's night market, Petra sells harmless trinkets while hiding the storm that crackles under his skin. A dying beggar's prayer is suddenly answered by an old god, and the miracle marks every magic-bearer in the city—including Petra. The emotional beat is dread: seven years of careful invisibility shatter in one night, and the city watch begins its hunt.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a flashback interlude in Maerin's voice. Fleeing Greyhollow, Petra finds his mother's sealed letters revealing the family bargain: Maerin's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to buy the storm-line's exile instead of execution. The beat is grief curdling into resolve—loyalty to his dead family means facing the truth he fled.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Disguised as a tithe-bearer, Petra infiltrates the underworld court during Vaelric's coronation feast above. He finds Maerin enthralled as the court's living archive, and the price of her release is a soul of equal weight. As Vaelric's armies march on the free cities, Petra signs himself into the ledger. The beat is sacrifice—love outweighing duty to self.

chapters.title: A Name Given Back
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV opening, shifting to Petra's. Freed but hollowed, Maerin carries Petra's nameless body out of the mountain as the gods themselves intervene, refusing the ledger's claim on a willing heart. Petra wakes stripped of storm-magic but bound to something older. The armies break against the free cities' renewed faith. The beat is quiet triumph: inheritance redefined as choice, not blood.
